Subfamily alignments

One row per subfamily. Links open 100-copy MAFFT alignments (50 bp left, 70 bp right flanks) in the MSA viewer: the consensus rebuilt from the copies is row 1, the consensus as searched is row 2. The alignments hold SINE loci (assigned copies whose flanks were tested unique) and, when a subfamily has fewer than 100 of them, its grey-zone copies (flanks masked as repeats or untestable), marked [grey]; the button then shows their count. Copies with shared flanks, or the same flank at the same place in many copies, and soft-assigned copies are never shown. The SINE loci column counts SINE loci (hover for the split into SINE / grey zone / not SINE); a subfamily whose flanks could not be tested keeps Grey zone as its overall call. Last four columns: automated SINE-discriminator checks on the top-100 view (Flanks, Flank context, Element, Overall).

Sequence similarity between consensuses

The sequence-part view of the hierarchy: which stretches of one consensus are similar to which stretches of another, from the sequences alone (ungapped blocks of at least 30 bp and 80 % identity, both strands, simple repeats masked). Each cell is the share of the row consensus (its length is given after the name) that lies in blocks shared with the column consensus; empty = no block. It is directional: a short consensus inside a long one is 100 % in that row and a small share in the other. Click a cell to see the two consensuses with their blocks.

Is the shorter one a separate SINE?

For every consensus that is the 5′ part of a longer one, the copies of both are tested: do they end at two separate places, do the bases inside follow the length, does each end have its own TSD (docs/LENGTH_VARIANTS.md).

Do the copies sit in tandem arrays?

Copies in a run of at least five on one contig with regular spacing (gaps up to 6 kb, within a factor of 5 of the run's median) are units of an array, not independent insertions. The share is compared with the same copies spread at random over the contigs (chance): a dense family forms regular runs by chance (VES in Taphozous, one copy per 3 kb, 56 % of its copies in runs, nearly all chance). A family whose share exceeds chance by 20 points or more is marked, and its plates take independent copies first (tools/array_flag.py).

Satellites: SINE sequence in tandem arrays

Before extraction and assignment, the hits of each consensus were screened for tandem arrays (docs/SATELLITES.md): loci where the monomer is a part of the SINE (TRF on the hit windows, unit aligned to the consensus, at least 4 monomers) and arrays of regular spacing whose unit is longer than the SINE; a regularly spaced run counts as an array when its units are near-identical (median unit identity ≥ 85 %, “verified”), whatever the family's share. 291 hits in satellite loci were removed from the SINE analysis (kept in excluded_hits.bed). Loci and monomer consensuses: results/satellites/.

Are the flanks of the copies unique?

Independent insertions have unrelated flanks. For every family the 100 bp next to each copy, read outward from the junction, are compared between all its firmly assigned copies (flank scan stage 9, flankscan/fs9_twins.sh); 20-mers that occur more than 20 times in the genome are masked first, so known repeats are never evidence. Two copies are twins when a flank is colinear and at least 85 % identical (tier 1) or 70 % (tier 2) over at least 50 bp from the junction on: segmental duplications, array units the satellite screen did not catch, copies carried inside another element. A copy with too few testable bases after masking is masked, one with a flank cut by a contig end untestable. Twin copies are marked [twin] on the plates and the top 100 takes one copy per twin group first.

Is each consensus what its copies say?

Every consensus is rebuilt from the copies assigned to it (random subsamples, two seeds) and compared with the bank sequence (docs/CONSENSUS_AUDIT.md). A shorter or longer rebuild is not an error by itself: it says that fewer, or more, than 30 % of the copies carry a stretch.

Do copies continue past their ends into another consensus?

Each copy is read with 150 bp on both sides; past the end of its own consensus's match the sequence is searched against the bank (tools/continuation_check.py, up to 400 copies per consensus, assigned copies and unassigned copies separately). A row is flagged when at least a fifth of the copies continue, from the junction on, into the same consensus (of the copies in which the own consensus was found, tested): then the copies are a longer element than their consensus, for example a composite the bank lacks. Inside locus tells how much of that continuation lies inside the copy's own coordinates: mostly inside = the copy carries the label of a shorter consensus; mostly outside = its coordinates stop early. For a flag a candidate consensus is built from those copies and compared with the bank. Nothing in the run is changed by this check.

No consensus is flagged (0 continuations below a fifth of the copies).

Where the heads come from: tRNA, 5S, 7SL

Every consensus, and under each composite every stretch of it as read by its units, compared with tRNA genes (ssearch36; the best tRNA, identity and its span), against 20 dinucleotide-preserving shuffles of the same sequence (bits / best shuffle), plus Rfam (Infernal cmscan) and tRNAscan-SE. A head is called tRNA-derived when the gene hit passes SINEBase's rule (≥ 60 % identity over ≥ 60 nt) and beats every shuffle; ? = beats the shuffles but below 60 / 60; 5S / 7SL from Rfam. Rfam and tRNAscan-SE miss degraded heads; their anticodon calls on such heads are noise (hover a chip for the measurements, including the next amino acid). Source: trna/trna_heads.tsv (tools/trna_heads.sh).

Overview

This run searched rmi.fna with 6 subfamily consensuses from bank6.fa. After merging overlapping hits across queries, 28,378 candidate SINE copies entered step2. Of those, 28,341 (99.9%) were unanimously called by all 10 sub-samples, 28,330 (99.8%) passed the bitscore threshold and received a final subfamily label, and 48 (0.2%) remained unassigned.

Flank verdict: of 28,330 assigned copies, 11,379 are SINE loci (flanks tested unique), 3,016 are in the grey zone (flanks masked as repeats or untestable) and 13,935 are not SINE loci (flanks shared with another copy, the same flank at the same place in many copies, or the subfamily's flanks still shared at the expansion limit). Copy numbers in the tables below count assigned copies; per-copy verdicts: step2/step2_output/loci_verdict.tsv.

Assembly check: SOLID (genome.clean_assembly_qc.tsv).

Divergence from consensus — per copy

Metric: divergence = 100 − ssearch36 %identity to the subfamily consensus (same as Gallery histograms). Copies binned at 1% divergence; line connects bin counts (smooth spline). One line per subfamily; click legend to hide/show.

Source: step4 *_pctid.tsv on assigned copies.

PCA — mutation landscape

Each point is one assigned SINE copy, coloured by subfamily. Axes are PC1 / PC2 of a binary mutation matrix: each alignment column where the copy nucleotide differs from its assigned-subfamily consensus is encoded as 1, matches as 0. Only variable columns (mutation rate 3–97 %) are used. Copies with distinct mutation patterns cluster together — subfamily clouds are expected when subfamilies have different characteristic mutations.

Method: mafft --add --keeplength adds sampled copies into the consensus alignment (up to 200 per subfamily). Binary mutation matrix → SVD. η²(subfamily→PC1) = fraction of PC1 variance explained by subfamily label (0 = no separation, 1 = perfect).

Bitscore thresholds vs consensus self-bits

Step2 bitscores are summed over the 10 voting cycles (a copy scoring 310 bits once has 3,100 here); the threshold is 0.45 × the N-th best copy's sum. Real self-bits = ssearch36 score of the consensus vs itself, one alignment. Threshold/Self (one cycle's share) ≈ the minimum fraction of the consensus self-score a copy must reach.

Column legend
  • Subfamily — Subfamily name.
  • Threshold (10-cycle sum) — Bitscore cutoff used by step2: 0.45 × the N-th best copy's bitscore, where step2 bitscores are summed over the 10 voting cycles.
  • RealSelfBits — ssearch36 bitscore of the consensus aligned against itself (one alignment, not summed).
  • Threshold/Self — Threshold divided by 10 (one cycle) / RealSelfBits. Roughly the minimum fraction of the consensus self-score a copy must reach (0.45 of the best copies' score). Before 2026-10-05 this column divided by 100 and read ten times too low.
